import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Henson graph

For $i \geq 3$, the Henson graph $G_i$ is the unique countable homogeneous graph that contains
no $i$-vertex clique but contains every finite $K_i$-free graph as an induced subgraph.
The first of them, $G_3$, is the homogeneous (or universal) triangle-free graph.

The question, due to Cherlin, asks whether the Henson graphs have the finite model property,
i.e. whether every first-order sentence (in the language of graphs) that holds in $G_i$ also holds
in some finite graph. In other words, is $G_i$ pseudofinite?

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Henson graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henson_graph)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [He71] C. Ward Henson, *A family of countable homogeneous graphs*,
  Pacific Journal of Mathematics 38 (1971), 69–83.
-/

namespace HensonGraph

open FirstOrder Language SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- A simple graph `G` on the vertex set `V` is a *Henson graph* `G_i` if it is countable,
contains no clique on `i` vertices, contains every finite `Kᵢ`-free graph as an induced subgraph,
and is homogeneous, i.e. every isomorphism between finite induced subgraphs of `G` extends to an
automorphism of `G` (this is `FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous` for the structure
`G.structure` in the language of graphs).

Such a graph exists and is unique up to isomorphism for every `i ≥ 3`; see [He71]. -/
structure IsHensonGraph (i : ℕ) : Prop where
  countable : Countable V
  cliqueFree : G.CliqueFree i
  universal : ∀ {W : Type} [Finite W] (H : SimpleGraph W), H.CliqueFree i → Nonempty (H ↪g G)
  ultrahomogeneous : letI := G.structure; Language.graph.IsUltrahomogeneous V

/-- A simple graph `G` has the *finite model property* (equivalently, `G` is *pseudofinite*) if
every first-order sentence in the language of graphs that holds in `G` also holds in some finite
simple graph. This says exactly that the complete first-order theory of `G` has the finite model
property. -/
def HasFiniteModelProperty : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : Language.graph.Sentence, (letI := G.structure; V ⊨ φ) →
    ∃ (W : Type) (H : SimpleGraph W), Finite W ∧ (letI := H.structure; W ⊨ φ)

/-- Every finite simple graph has the finite model property. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 5]
theorem hasFiniteModelProperty_of_finite [Finite V] : HasFiniteModelProperty G :=
  fun _ hφ => ⟨V, G, inferInstance, hφ⟩

/-- A Henson graph `G_i` with `i ≥ 2` is infinite, since it contains every finite edgeless graph
as an induced subgraph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsHensonGraph.infinite {i : ℕ} (hi : 2 ≤ i) (hG : IsHensonGraph G i) : Infinite V := by
  refine Infinite.of_not_fintype fun _ => ?_
  obtain ⟨f⟩ := hG.universal (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin (Fintype.card V + 1))) (cliqueFree_bot hi)
  have := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f f.injective
  simp at this

/-- Do the Henson graphs have the finite model property? That is, for every `i ≥ 3`, does every
first-order sentence in the language of graphs that holds in the Henson graph `G_i` also hold in
some finite graph? -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem henson_graph :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (i : ℕ), 3 ≤ i → ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsHensonGraph G i →
      HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

/-- Does the homogeneous (universal) triangle-free graph `G_3` have the finite model property?
That is, does every first-order sentence in the language of graphs that holds in `G_3` also hold
in some finite graph? -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem henson_graph.variants.triangle_free :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsHensonGraph G 3 →
      HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

end HensonGraph

modeling_decisions: The list-page entry is terse; the precise formulation is taken from the article's definition of G_i (unique countable homogeneous K_i-free graph containing all finite K_i-free graphs as induced subgraphs) plus the standard model-theoretic meaning of 'finite model property' for the complete theory Th(G_i): every sentence true in G_i has a finite model (G_i is pseudofinite). This is the sense of Cherlin's question; the alternative reading 'Th(G_i) is axiomatised by its finite models' would be trivially false since Th(G_i) has no finite models, so it is not the intended one.

The finite model is required to be a finite simple graph (rather than an arbitrary finite structure in the graph language). This is equivalent: if φ holds in G one may conjoin the (finitely many) graph axioms, which also hold in G, so any finite model of the conjunction is a graph.

Instead of constructing G_i, the theorem quantifies over all graphs on a `Type` (universe 0) vertex set satisfying `IsHensonGraph G i`. Since such graphs exist (Henson 1971) and are unique up to isomorphism (Fraïssé), and pseudofiniteness is isomorphism-invariant, this is equivalent to the statement about 'the' Henson graph G_i; the quantifier is not vacuous.

Homogeneity is expressed with Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous Language.graph V` under `G.structure`. Primary statement quantifies over all i ≥ 3 with a single `answer(sorry)`, as the plural 'the Henson graphs' asks about all of them; `answer(True)` means every G_i is pseudofinite, `answer(False)` means some G_i is not.

namespace HensonGraph

open FirstOrder Language

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A simple graph `G` on the vertex type `V` is a *Henson graph* `G_i` if `V` is countable and `G`
is `K_i`-free, ultrahomogeneous (every isomorphism between finite induced subgraphs of `G` extends
to an automorphism of `G`), and universal for finite `K_i`-free graphs (every finite `K_i`-free
graph is an induced subgraph of `G`).

Henson (1971) showed that for every `i ≥ 3` such a graph exists and is unique up to isomorphism.
Ultrahomogeneity is expressed via `FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous` for the
`Language.graph`-structure `G.structure` associated to `G`. -/
structure _root_.SimpleGraph.IsHensonGraph (i : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop where
  countable : Countable V
  cliqueFree : G.CliqueFree i
  isUltrahomogeneous : @Language.graph.IsUltrahomogeneous V G.structure
  universal : ∀ (W : Type) [Finite W] (H : SimpleGraph W), H.CliqueFree i → Nonempty (H ↪g G)

/-- For `i ≥ 2`, a Henson graph `G_i` has infinitely many vertices, since it contains every
finite edgeless graph as an induced subgraph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem _root_.SimpleGraph.IsHensonGraph.infinite {i : ℕ} (hi : 2 ≤ i) {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (hG : G.IsHensonGraph i) : Infinite V := by
  refine not_finite_iff_infinite.mp fun hV ↦ ?_
  obtain ⟨f⟩ := hG.universal (Fin (Nat.card V + 1)) ⊥ (SimpleGraph.cliqueFree_bot hi)
  have := Nat.card_le_card_of_injective f f.injective
  simp at this

/-- A first-order structure `M` for a language `L` is *pseudofinite*, i.e. its complete theory
`L.completeTheory M` has the *finite model property*, if every `L`-sentence true in `M` is also
true in some finite `L`-structure. -/
def _root_.FirstOrder.Language.IsPseudofinite (L : Language) (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] :
    Prop :=
  ∀ φ : L.Sentence, M ⊨ φ → ∃ (N : Type) (_ : L.Structure N), Finite N ∧ N ⊨ φ

/-- A finite structure is pseudofinite. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem _root_.FirstOrder.Language.IsPseudofinite.of_finite (L : Language) (M : Type)
    [L.Structure M] [Finite M] : L.IsPseudofinite M :=
  fun _ h ↦ ⟨M, inferInstance, inferInstance, h⟩

/-- **Henson graphs and the finite model property.**
Do the Henson graphs have the finite model property? That is, for every `i ≥ 3` and every Henson
graph `G_i` (the unique countable homogeneous `K_i`-free graph that is universal for finite
`K_i`-free graphs), is every first-order sentence in the language of graphs that is true in `G_i`
also true in some finite structure? Equivalently, is the complete theory of `G_i` pseudofinite?
Since a finite model of such a sentence may be taken to satisfy the (first-order) graph axioms as
well, the finite models may equivalently be required to be finite graphs. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem henson_graph :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ i ≥ 3, ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsHensonGraph i →
      @Language.graph.IsPseudofinite V G.structure := by
  sorry

/-- **The homogeneous triangle-free graph and the finite model property.**
The case `i = 3` of `henson_graph`: does the Henson graph `G_3`, also called the homogeneous
(or universal, or generic) triangle-free graph, have the finite model property? That is, is every
first-order sentence in the language of graphs that is true in `G_3` also true in some finite
structure? This is Cherlin's question of whether the generic triangle-free graph is pseudofinite. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem henson_graph.variants.triangle_free :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsHensonGraph 3 →
      @Language.graph.IsPseudofinite V G.structure := by
  sorry

end HensonGraph

`Countable V` (rather than countably infinite) is used, matching 'countable' in the source; infiniteness follows from universality for i ≥ 2.

Quantification over the vertex type uses `∀ (V : Type*)` inside the statement (universe-polymorphic theorem); since a countable type lives, up to equivalence, in any universe this does not change the content.

The range `i ≥ 3` follows the article ('for all i ≥ 3'); the plural 'the Henson graphs' is read as a single question about all of them, with one `answer(sorry)`, as the decomposition table prescribes.

namespace HensonGraph

/-- A Henson graph of index `i` is a countably infinite, ultrahomogeneous, $K_i$-free
simple graph into which every finite $K_i$-free simple graph embeds as an induced subgraph. -/
def IsHensonGraph (i : ℕ) {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Countable V ∧ Infinite V ∧ G.CliqueFree i ∧
    @FirstOrder.Language.IsUltrahomogeneous FirstOrder.Language.graph V G.structure ∧
    ∀ {W : Type} [Finite W] (H : SimpleGraph W), H.CliqueFree i → Nonempty (H ↪g G)

/-- A simple graph has the finite model property (is pseudofinite) if every first-order sentence
in the language of graphs which is true in it is also true in a finite nonempty simple graph. -/
def HasFiniteModelProperty {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FirstOrder.Language.graph.Sentence,
    @FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize FirstOrder.Language.graph V G.structure φ →
      ∃ (W : Type) (_ : Finite W) (_ : Nonempty W) (H : SimpleGraph W),
        @FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize FirstOrder.Language.graph W H.structure φ

/--
Do all Henson graphs have the finite model property? Precisely, is it true for every index
$i \ge 3$ that every first-order graph-language sentence true in the Henson graph $G_i$ has
a finite nonempty simple graph model?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem henson_graph : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (i : ℕ), 3 ≤ i → ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsHensonGraph i G → HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

universal triangle-free graph, have the finite model property? Equivalently, does every
first-order graph-language sentence true in $G_3$ have a finite nonempty simple graph model?
-/

theorem triangle_free : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V), IsHensonGraph 3 G → HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

end henson_graph.variants

end HensonGraph

This is equivalent to allowing arbitrary finite `Language.graph`-structures because the graph axioms (irreflexive, symmetric) are true in G_i, so φ ∧ axioms ∈ Th(G_i) has a finite model iff φ has a finite graph model.

The Henson graph is captured by a characterizing predicate `IsHensonGraph i G` rather than a concrete construction (Henson's construction via the Rado graph is not in Mathlib). # Henson graphs

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Henson graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henson_graph)

namespace HensonGraph

/-- `IsHensonGraph i G` says that `G` is an infinite countable homogeneous $K_i$-free graph
that is universal for finite $K_i$-free graphs. Homogeneity means that every isomorphism between
finite induced subgraphs extends to an automorphism of `G`. -/
def IsHensonGraph {V : Type*} (i : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Infinite V ∧ Countable V ∧ G.CliqueFree i ∧
    (∀ (W : Type) [Finite W] (H : SimpleGraph W), H.CliqueFree i → Nonempty (H ↪g G)) ∧
    ∀ (s t : Set V), s.Finite → t.Finite → ∀ e : G.induce s ≃g G.induce t,
      ∃ a : G ≃g G, ∀ x : s, a x = e x

/-- A graph has the finite model property here if every first-order sentence in the language of
graphs that is true in the graph has a nonempty finite graph model. -/
def HasFiniteModelProperty {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  letI := G.structure
  ∀ φ : FirstOrder.Language.graph.Sentence, V ⊨ φ →
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      letI := H.structure
      Fin n ⊨ φ

/-- Do all Henson graphs $G_i$, for $i \geq 3$, have the finite model property? That is, is every
first-order graph sentence true in such a $G_i$ also true in some nonempty finite graph? -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem henson_graph :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ i ≥ 3, ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsHensonGraph i G → HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

theorem henson_graph.variants.triangle_free :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsHensonGraph 3 G → HasFiniteModelProperty G := by
  sorry

end HensonGraph
